svg.title: Every complex projective-plane Lie algebra
svg.desc: Irreducible matrix actions are the full sl3 algebra or the three-dimensional conic stabilizer. Reducible nonsolvable actions give six affine or block models. Every solvable action preserves a complete flag and lies in its five-dimensional stabilizer; projection onto the affine x-line and all vertical kernels give the complete covering list.
svg.text: The complete projective-plane reduction
h ⊂ pgl₃(ℂ) ≅ sl₃(ℂ), acting on ℙ(ℂ³); ordinary projective conjugacy first.
Does the matrix action preserve a proper nonzero subspace of ℂ³?
A matrix line is a projective point; a matrix plane is a projective line.
No: irreducible
Every solvable ideal acts by scalars, hence is zero.
A maximal toral algebra has dimension 1 or 2.
rank 1: C₃, the nonsingular conic stabilizer
rank 2: full sl₃, dimension 8
Yes: reducible
A point or a line is invariant.
Point and line cases are exchanged by duality.
Separate nonsolvable and solvable actions.
Ordinary projective types remain distinct.
Reducible and nonsolvable: six types
A preserved line gives affine matrices (L,b) ∈ gl₂ ⋉ ℂ².
The image is sl₂ or gl₂; its translation kernel is 0 or ℂ².
Full kernel: A₅, A₆ and their duals. Zero kernel: L₃, L₄ (self-dual).
The zero-kernel graph is removed by the explicit equation β([L,K]) = Lβ(K) − Kβ(L).
Solvable: an incident point / line flag is invariant
Choose the line at infinity and its vertical point: b = ⟨p,q,R,A,B⟩, R = xq.
Projection onto the affine x-line:
image 0
image ⟨p⟩ or ⟨A⟩
image ⟨p,A⟩
The vertical kernel lies in k = ⟨q,R,B⟩. Its complete list is:
A kernel with a nonconstant translation coefficient forces its root to be fixed by the image.
Lemma 8.8 solves every lift and every residual bracket, including resonant coefficients.
Changing the flag gives the final projective parameter relations
F₄(a,c), K₂(a,c): [a:c] exact. T₃(a,c): [a:c] ~ [c:a].
W₃(a,c): [a:c] ~ [a:a−c]. One-dimensional distinct eigenvalues: six values.
Nilpotent ranks, common kernels/images and Jordan parts separate all remaining types.
No seven-dimensional algebra occurs; zero and the full algebra are included.
Proof: Lemmas 8.6–8.8 and Theorem 8.9. Exact dual pairings: Corollary 8.10.
The schematic concerns complex connected local projective actions and their matrix algebras.
